text:
Vikram: Bringing back the phased-commit idea from the RFC — thinking about a lightweight two-phase handshake for streaming requests so we can safely retry midstream without re-executing heavy model work. want quick sanity check on tradeoffs.

Cassie: short version of the proposal?

Vikram: admit -> stream-commit -> finalize. admit reserves a slot + gives an ephemeral commit token. stream-commit is sent once first non-idempotent output is produced; token proves work already started so retries can fast-path to resume vs restart. finalize closes lifecycle.

Jordan: hmm. how does this interact with client TCP drops and reconnects? if client reconnects but doesn't have the token, they can re-admit and we might duplicate work unless we checkpoint kv cache.

Vikram: yep. two options: 1) short-lived token TTL + prefix-KV checkpointing (small resume window), 2) make stream-commit idempotent by storing minimal resume state at edge for O(seconds) and accept duplicate compute for lower complexity.

Anya: what's the memory footprint of storing resume state at edge? we can't keep KV per request for minutes.

Vikram: target is small: only last N cached KV pages + sequence pointer, ~1-2KB per active stream. with admission limits and LRU expiry that's manageable for hosted, but dedicated/private may need config to disable resume caching.

Cassie: is there an API header sketch? I worry about client compat.

Vikram: thinking `x-rw-commit-phase: admit|commit|final` plus `x-rw-commit-token` on commit/final. example:``
> POST /v1/generate
> x-rw-commit-phase: admit
> body: { prompt }

> POST /v1/generate
> x-rw-commit-phase: commit
> x-rw-commit-token: abc123
> stream: chunk...
```

Jordan: that looks fine. how do we handle multi-hop proxies? token must be opaque but verifiable across frontdoor -> compute -> cache. do we sign tokens with edge key?

Anya: signing is ok but adds key management. alternative is transactional lease ID stored in central store keyed to request id; edge looks up lease. tradeoff: central lookup cost vs crypto verify.

Cassie: for performance we should avoid a blocking lookup on every commit. maybe a hybrid: short signed token (HMAC) validated locally, plus a central reconciliation async job for GC and audit.

Vikram: agreed. signed token with TTL, include shard id so only relevant edge verifies. central store used for long-tail reconciliation and debugging.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: rolling canary of edge-token-key v2 scheduled for 2026-05-12 03:00 UTC.

Jordan: what about retries semantics? if an upstream gateway retries with same token, should compute dedupe or resume?

Vikram: semantics: if commit-token presented and resume state exists -> resume. if token presented but resume state expired -> treat as commit without resume (start from clean state) but record 'stale-token' metric and annotate response with `x-rw-resume-hint: stale`. if no token -> normal admit flow.

Anya: that makes sense, but we need explicit SLOs: resume window default = 8s, configurable per-customer for Dedicated. if you want longer you pay for retention or use Dedicated with stronger guarantees.

Cassie: observability: expose commit_attempts, resume_hits, resume_misses, stale_token_rate, avg_resume_recovery_latency. add a per-request trace id to link admit->commit->finalize spans.

Jordan: fallback story for mobile clients with flaky connections? mobile SDK should store token and backoff retries. but also server should accept re-admits: lightweight re-admit path that returns 409+resume-hint instead of forcing re-exec.

Vikram: exactly. re-admit returns either 200(admitted) or 409(already-committed) with `x-rw-commit-token` and best-effort resume position. clients can then reconnect and `commit` with token.

Cassie: security note: tokens must be scoped to request and not leak instructions/state. rotate keys and include nonce.

Anya: one more operational hitch: control-plane disconnects during finalize could leave stale state. need GC and idempotent finalize that tolerates repeated finalize calls.

Vikram: finalize must be idempotent and gated by token. also an async GC that cleans resume state after TTL+buffer. record metrics for finalize_retries.

Jordan: i'm worried about added complexity for edge runtime. could we implement an opt-in mode: new API param `resume=true` default false? roll out opt-in -> gated by tenant.

Vikram: good call. default off, enable per-tenant flag, gradually flip on for high-throughput workloads where cost of duplicate compute is high. config surfaces in Redwood Console under routing/policies.

Cassie: ok i'm on board. next steps?

Vikram: i'll draft a follow-up doc with state diagram, token format (HMAC with shard+nonce+exp), minimal edge state blob shape, metrics list, and per-tenant config knobs. will ping for reviews.

Anya: add a small perf test plan: fire N connections with induced reconnections and measure cost saved vs duplication.

Jordan: and a security review for token leaks.

Cassie: :thumbsup: thanks, Vikram.
